consumers.evidence: README defines first-scan pairing, durable trusted-device behavior, repeated-scan identity reuse, stable-origin migration, direct reopen, and revocation.
Structured user-confirmed decision LAN-TRUSTED-DEVICE-001 records confirmed and deferred scope.
The fixed 30-day server expiry remains removed, QR tickets are one-time, and an already trusted browser refreshes or adopts its existing identity instead of creating a duplicate device.

Implementation commits 3c97bac and 0ffa34c contain the persistent device registry, rolling browser session, local device-management API/UI, revocation, repeated-scan reuse, origin-migration adoption, and tests.

checks.evidence: Server and client typechecks passed on 2026-08-27 against implementation commit 0ffa34c.

checks.name: Unit tests
checks.evidence: Twelve test files and thirty-three tests passed, including persistent trusted-device, revocation, repeated-scan reuse, one-time pairing tickets, and cross-origin identity adoption.

checks.name: Production trusted-device restart probe
checks.command: pair -> authenticate -> restart -> authenticate -> revoke -> reject
checks.evidence: A temporary device authenticated before and after a production service restart, failed immediately after revocation, and was removed without changing the nine existing trusted devices on 2026-08-27.

checks.name: Production repeated-scan and origin-migration probe
checks.command: pair -> rescan same QR -> adopt stable-link ticket in fresh origin session -> authenticate -> revoke
checks.evidence: The trusted-device count moved from 10 to 11 on first pairing, stayed 11 after rescanning the same QR, stayed 11 after a fresh-origin session adopted the stable-link identity, authenticated successfully, and returned to 10 after removing the temporary device on 2026-08-27.
